metkar2012.cite: P. S. Metkar, "Experimental and Kinetic Modeling Studies of Selective Catalytic Reduction of NOx with NH3 on Fe- and Cu-Zeolite Monolithic Catalysts", PhD dissertation, University of Houston, 2012 (advisors M. P. Harold and V. Balakotaiah).
metkar2012.conditions: Steady state after about 25 min per point, 1000 sccm total in Ar, GHSV about 57,000 1/h (thesis p. 333 and ch. 9). Pretreated at 500 C in 5% O2. FTIR analyzer (MKS MultiGas 2030).

xie2026.cite: X. Xie, J. Yuan, L. Liu, H. Liu and Z. Sun, "Dual kinetic effect from confined iron nanoparticles in zeolite modulates high-temperature catalytic NO reduction and NH3 oxidation", Ind. Chem. Mater. 4 (2026) 457-471, doi:10.1039/d5im00245a. Open access under CC BY-NC 4.0.
xie2026.conditions: Quartz fixed bed, 2 L/min, GHSV 30,000 1/h, IR analyzer, each point averaged over 20 min at steady state. SCR feed 1000 ppm NO, 1000 ppm NH3, 6% O2, N2 balance, no water. Ammonia oxidation runs feed 500 ppm NH3: the figures give 140 ppm NH3 left and a 5% NOx share at 700 C, and 20 ppm NOx out, which only a 500 ppm feed fits (Fig. 3c against Fig. 5b-c).

odenbrand2017.cite: C. U. I. Odenbrand, "High Temperature and High Concentration SCR of NO with NH3 for the Oxyfuel Combustion Process: Fitting of Kinetics to Data from a Laboratory Reactor Experiment", Top. Catal. 60 (2017) 1317-1332, doi:10.1007/s11244-017-0817-x. Open access under CC BY 4.0.
odenbrand2017.conditions: Gold-plated steel fixed bed at 2.2 bar, 180 NL/h (GHSV 120,000 1/h at NTP), steady state after 10-45 min. Oxyfuel flue-gas feed: 5000 ppm NO, 5500 ppm NH3, 13.06% O2, 5.03% H2O (N2 balance in the paper's model). Inlet stepped from 570 to 800 K in 25 K steps; each point is plotted at the bed-exit temperature. Ammonia is scrubbed out before the analyzers: NO by chemiluminescence, N2O by NDIR.
